observations:
Torah #174 contains zero bechina edges in the dataset and zero bechina-language statements in the source text. The framework criterion for a new package is: 3+ bechina-connected concepts forming an independent domain not captured by existing packages. Since no bechina connections exist at all in this Torah — neither in the dataset nor in the source text — the threshold of 3+ bechina-connected concepts cannot be met by definition. No new package is warranted.

The only candidate that was examined was the gematria equivalence 'נָא רְפָא = מִרְיָם יוֹכֶבֶד' — which could superficially appear to link the prayer-phrase to the name-pair. However, this is explicitly characterized in the text as a רֶמֶז נִפְלָא (a wonderful cryptographic hint using numerical values), not a בְּחִינַת (a shared-nature identity). Gematria is a homiletical tool for concealment; bechina is a structural assertion of co-essential nature. These are categorically different. The framework (§1.1) defines bechina as 'two concepts shar[ing] the same essential nature, quality, or dimension — different expressions of the same underlying reality.' A gematria remez meets none of these criteria.

The teaching's conceptual vocabulary — דינין (judgments), שם (name), מקטרגים (accusers), תפלה (prayer), רמז (hint), גימטריא (gematria) — are all present in their causal/procedural roles without any bechina identification. Even if one were to cluster 'name-mentioning in prayer' + 'judgments' + 'accusers' as a thematic family, their only connections in the text are eitza (causal-conditional), not bechina (parallel-nature). A package built on eitza connections would violate framework §3.2 rule 2: 'Built on bechinas only — packages are formed from bechina-connected nodes, not eitza edges.'

Conclusion: Torah #174 is structurally incapable of generating packages or new packages. It is a short practical ruling with no bechina topology.
